ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, under the condition that light and other conditions are suitable for plants A and B, the response characteristics of photosynthesis intensity to changes in CO2 concentration in the environment are shown. According to the figure, if the seedlings of the above two plants are placed in the same sealed glass cover, under the condition that light and other conditions are suitable, within a period of time, which plant's growth will be affected first?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the horizontal axis is labeled CO2 concentration, and the vertical axis is labeled net CO2 fixation amount or photosynthesis intensity. Curve A rises rapidly at a relatively low CO2 concentration and reaches a nearly stable plateau relatively early; curve B has a relatively low value under low CO2 concentration, and only gradually strengthens as CO2 concentration increases, requiring a higher CO2 concentration to reach a higher photosynthesis intensity. Then reason: if the seedlings of the two plants are placed in the same sealed glass cover, when light and other conditions are suitable, the plants' continuous photosynthesis will consume the CO2 inside the cover, causing the environmental CO2 concentration to gradually decrease. As CO2 decreases, the plant whose photosynthesis decreases more obviously under low CO2 conditions and is more sensitive to CO2 reduction will be limited first. It can be seen from the figure that B's photosynthesis intensity under low CO2 concentration is obviously lower than A's, indicating that B has a weaker ability to adapt to low CO2, so the growth that is affected first is B.
